main_text.l: Putrefactio est, quando partes terreæ in aqueo
copioso consistentes, calore externo in ipso hu-
mido crassescente rarefiunt ; atq; ita utraq; ob
pugnam primarum qualitatum corruptionem
quandam experiuntur.
unde plerunq; initiò ingratum odorem pu-

Bruta corpora per putrefactionem genita sunt, mine-
ralia & metalla.
Mineralia, quorum humidū supra terreum sic-
cum exsuperat : Sal, alumen; & bitumen.
Sal est minerale, ex pauciore terreo, in copio-
siore aqueo minùs crasso, per vehementè calore
adusto, & cum eo indurato, genitum.
unde Sal humido frigido potissimùm facile
liquescit.
Sal in terris aliud, aliud in aquis nascitur.

page.notes: Decorative flourish before "Atq;" in the heading is ornament, not text. Small mark at the foot centre is uncertain and is recorded as a possible signature "4[?]". Catchword "In" sits at the lower right. The line "unde plerunq;" and the word "putrescentia" are split at a line end with a printed hyphen, kept as printed. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout, including where it resembles f in "trescentia" and "crasso" as printed.
